title: Facial fractures and the long-term risk of mental health complications
html: The psychosocial implications of facial fractures are unclear. The aim of the study was to identify any association between facial fractures and the long-term risk of hospitalization for mental health disorders. The study followed a cohort of 64,089 patients aged ≥10 years who were hospitalized for facial fractures between 1989 and 2023 in Quebec, Canada. Patients with facial fractures were matched to 318,520 controls based on age, sex, and year, and facial fractures were classified by site, type, and cause.
